items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, Exploration design session); Claude (written into EXPLORATION.md)
items.title: Spend is estimated once at 1960 and seeds the campaign's depletion reserve
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-11): "For depletion accounting, I would prefer if we retrofit this, and come to a sensible estimate at the very end of digitisation. For generation you are right in that keeping items abstract is best policy." So NO ACCUMULATOR IS ADDED anywhere in the history sim, and sprint 39's closed Empire span is NOT reopened.

WHY IT MATTERS. Ben, 2026-09-11, on what digitisation passes forward: "the main levers we pass are going to be about how much of easily accessible resource has been actually spent." The saturated corporate web forms around what is LEFT.

WHERE IT LANDS IS ALREADY BUILT, AND THIS IS THE ELEGANT PART. `tile_component::resource_remaining` (components.hpp) is a finite reserve, live, drawn down by extraction and tapering output as it empties -- and it is SEEDED AT GENERATION to richness x a reserve factor (tile_generation.cpp). The two economy phases set that seed instead of a constant. Ground worked for centuries hands the campaign a thinner reserve. No new field, no new accumulator, no change to the campaign's extraction loop.

THE PRICE OF RETROFITTING, STATED PLAINLY AND ACCEPTED. An estimate computed once at 1960 can NEVER BE CHECKED against what actually happened, because nothing recorded it. That makes it a STATED FORMULA rather than a measurement. THE FORMULA MUST THEREFORE BE WRITTEN DOWN AS ONE -- named inputs, named arithmetic, in DIGITISATION.md -- or it silently becomes a fudge factor nobody can audit. Writing it down IS the work; an unwritten estimate is the failure mode.

ITS INPUTS ARE THE ABSTRACT ONES THE SIM ALREADY HOLDS: how long ground was held and worked, its `dominant` region class, whether it industrialised and when, and the corridor throughput that ran off it (BL-940).

PARKED UNTIL DIGITISATION IS DESIGNED. DIGITISATION.md is a placeholder by Ben's ruling; this item is filed now so the decision is not lost, and it is NOT sprint 40 work.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-13, live review); Claude (itemised)
items.title: A speed control (45s / 90s / 180s) on every lapse round's time-lapse, default 90 seconds
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-13: time-lapses currently run too fast to observe what is happening. Target the FULL playback (start year to end year, unskipped) at 90 seconds by default, and add a speed-control element present in EVERY lapse round (Culture, Empires, and the new Exploration round from BL-946) offering three settings: 45 seconds, 90 seconds, 180 seconds -- the user can also already skip ahead or scrub via the existing playhead/scrubber, this control is about the AUTOPLAY rate, not a replacement for scrubbing.

WHERE THE RATE LIVES TODAY. Find whatever currently drives year-per-frame or year-per-second in `history_lapse.cpp`'s playback (a fixed constant, most likely) and make it a function of (span length in years) / (chosen duration in seconds), recomputed whenever the round's span or the chosen duration changes -- a round with a longer span at the same duration setting must move faster per frame, not take longer wall-clock time, since the target is WALL-CLOCK duration, not years-per-second.

THE CONTROL ITSELF. Three-way selector (45s / 90s / 180s), same visual language as other wizard toggles (Sparse/Lean/Standard on the main menu is the nearest precedent for a three-way radio-style control). Persisted per-session is fine; it does not need to survive a restart unless that's trivial. Update `docs/ai/ACTIONS.json` for the new control and `docs/ui/question_log.json` for the surface it lives on.

DONE WHEN: all three lapse rounds (Culture, Empires, Exploration) expose the same speed control; selecting 45s/90s/180s visibly changes the playback rate; the default is 90s; a live click confirms the control is reachable and does what it says.

items.author: Claude (sprint 41 T2 finding, BL-956)
items.title: world_determinism digest covers seeded sentiment and stamped road tiers
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-14 by sprint 41 T2 (BL-956, Exploration handoff crosses). BL-956 moved world setup from 1200 CE grudges and corridors to 1660 ones: on seed ABCDEF01 sentiment seeding went from the 1200 grudge set to 76 rows off 225 grudges, and stamped corridors from 1664 to 2276 (612 new). Every world_determinism digest stayed digit-identical, because the digest reads neither `world::sentiment` nor road tiers. A contract that cannot see a change of that size is the same defect memory records for trade (goldens cannot see convoy traffic): the determinism check proves same-seed-same-world only for the parts it hashes.

WORK: fold seeded sentiment (sorted pairs and values) and the road tier per tile (or a per-tier tile count per body) into the deep digest. This moves every digest once: per DELIVERY.md sec The digest re-bless is one act per WAVE it is an authorised re-bless with the movement described (what the digest now covers), in its own commit, never folded into a world-moving item.

DONE WHEN: world_determinism fails when sentiment seeding or road stamping changes (demonstrate by a deliberate one-row perturbation run locally, not committed), and the re-bless is authorised by Ben.

items.author: Claude (sprint 41 wave 3 finding, BL-949)
items.title: The Empires span's try_upgrade_corridor writes its promotion into the corridor record
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-14 by sprint 41 wave 3 (BL-949, road rung fires). The Exploration span's post road set the live use count to the tier threshold but appended one row to the corridor record, so the record under-read the tier; BL-949 fixed it by carrying `history_corridor::tier`. `try_upgrade_corridor` in the EMPIRES span has the same one-row shape: the carried tier is now right, but `uses` still under-reads for any consumer that reads traffic rather than tier. Not fixed in sprint 41 because it moves the 1960/two-span digest, which the sprint kept unchanged by design.

WORK: make the Empires promotion write its uses consistently with the tier it grants (or document `uses` as traffic-only and audit every reader to use `tier`). Report the 1960 and seedA/off digest movement; re-bless only with authorisation.

items.author: Claude (2026-09-15 generation audit, five parallel readers); Ben chose A) file, B) build the harness library, then build
items.title: Planetology stores its thermal history as a per-epoch series so the Life phase can sample it
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-15 (physical-stage audit). theta_at, the past-thermal reconstructor, is a lambda inside run_planetology and is deliberately not exported; CONTINENTS.md states it as a boundary. BL-764 (Lagrangian tiles) was cancelled in the 2026-09-08 purge with only its query half shipped, so the Life phase's fossil placement reads the drift record for position but has no past climate to read. GENERATION_STRATEGY.md's fifth reorder call, "Life samples the real drift history", is half met.

WORK: expose the thermal history as a stored series on planetology_state, one value per drift epoch (the 20-epoch clock CONTINENTS.md already defines), derived not rolled, consuming no RNG. The palaeo pre-pass in tile_generation.cpp (~:2073-2145) reads it for the coal and oil epochs instead of proxying from the present. Serialised inline with the rest of planetology_state.

DONE WHEN: planetology_harness asserts the series is deterministic and epoch 0 equals the present value; deposit_origin D6 (withholding the drift record moves fossils) still holds and a second check shows withholding the thermal series moves them too; world_determinism digests move once, re-blessed with the movement described.

items.author: Claude (2026-09-15 generation audit, five parallel readers); Ben chose A) file, B) build the harness library, then build
items.title: The banding pass reads plate-carried position, so palaeo climate is a frame rather than a present-grid lookup
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-15. BL-764's frame half was cancelled in the purge, not on merit. Pass 3 still bands by present raster row (tile_generation.cpp:307-360); paleo_tile_at is a query over a finished world with four stated blind spots (CONTINENTS.md § The boundary of the frame). Ben's reorder call 5 (2026-09-03) chose the expensive answer deliberately.

WORK: the largest item in this set. The drift clock already yields a plate position per epoch; make Pass 3 (and the Life phase's palaeo pre-pass) read latitude and band from the plate-carried position at the sampled epoch rather than from the grid row. Keep epoch 0 bit-identical to the present (continent_drift C1 must hold). No RNG. Cost budgeted against home_surface_bench's 1 s ceiling.

DONE WHEN: continent_drift P-rows extend to a band-at-epoch check; deposit_origin D6 moves more ground than today and the world census concentration figures are re-read; home_surface_bench stays under its ceiling; digests re-blessed once with the movement described. Split into slices if the first measurement says the frame costs more than the ceiling allows.

items.author: Claude (2026-09-15 generation audit, five parallel readers); Ben chose A) file, B) build the harness library, then build
items.title: generate_body_tiles splits so the Life phase re-runs over a cached generation_record without the five passes above it
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-15. generate_body_tiles is one monolithic function running Passes 1-6 plus 4b-4e. Tuning a coal or peat rule costs a full 45,240-tile regeneration, and the census that shows the effect runs 120 seeds, so one Life-phase change costs 120 full surfaces. The generation_record seam already carries every intermediate the Life phase needs (heights, moisture, bands, body_phase_placed).

WORK: split the function at the Body/Life boundary into two callable halves with the record as the seam; the whole stays bit-identical. Add generate_life_deposits_over(record, ...) as the re-entry, and let earthlike_tile_census cache the Body half per seed in memory and re-run only the Life half when a --life-only flag is passed. No on-disk format; in-process reuse first.

DONE WHEN: tile_height_retention and world_determinism digests are unchanged; the census with --life-only produces identical fossil counts to a full run and completes in a fraction of the time (report the ratio).

items.author: Claude (2026-09-15 generation audit, five parallel readers); Ben chose A) file, B) build the harness library, then build
items.title: The migration walk prices rivers as corridors, as COLONISATION.md already claims
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-15. COLONISATION.md § Coastal and overseas routes says river courses and the coastal shelf are cheap; colonisation.hpp:555-571 prices the shoreline only and says in its own comment that the walk cannot yet price a river, "a real gap against" a world whose corridors are rivers. River edges exist as bitmasks (river_edges / river_downstream) since the rivers sibling pass.

WORK: read the river edge mask in the walk's step cost; a step along a river edge takes the coastal discount (one constant, shared, not a new dial). Downstream cheaper than upstream is NOT in scope unless the doc is amended first.

DONE WHEN: colonisation_harness gains a check that a cradle on a river reaches inland ground earlier than the same cradle with the river masked; C3/C3c (route not Voronoi) still hold; the split census is re-read and reported.

items.author: Claude (2026-09-15 generation audit, five parallel readers); Ben chose A) file, B) build the harness library, then build
items.title: Cultures that never hold ground are measured, and either merge back or stop being coined
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-15 (DEVLOG 2026-09-11 left-open list): about 95% of coined cultures never hold ground. The split census counts them as diversity; the Empires round and the lineage palette inherit thousands of names that mean nothing on the map, and culture_kinship_years walks a tree most of whose leaves are empty.

WORK, in two steps. (1) MEASURE: history_sweep and colonisation_harness print cultures coined, cultures holding at least one region at the boundary, and the ratio, per seed. (2) Then ONE of: fold an empty culture back into its parent at the boundary (shares reassigned, lineage kept), or gate coining on a minimum settled footprint. Which one is Ben's call and is filed in NEEDS_REVIEW when step 1's numbers are on the table; do not pick silently.

DONE WHEN: the reading is printed; the chosen rule is built; the lineage tree still walks back to a cradle (C14); the round-3 lapse shows fewer, larger kin hues, live-clicked.

items.author: Claude (2026-09-15 generation audit, five parallel readers); Ben chose A) file, B) build the harness library, then build
items.title: Navies and standing armies cost a per-head upkeep from the treasury, replacing the scorer caps
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-15; the call is NR-866 (open). BL-955's allocation scores a navy step 0 above 400 per held region and an army step 0 above 300 paid heads per held region; without the army cap polities bought an army every round. EXPLORATION.md § Force persists says upkeep is a cost in the world, not a handicap in the scorer, and the standing rule prefers systemic forces. Paid heads also cost no population, so a 44-region realm holds 13,200 heads for free and saturates neighbours' Alarm. NR-861 (treaties almost never break: 4 in 5,161) is the same shape: nothing drains a treasury enough to make defection worth it.

WORK: (1) a per-head running cost for army and navy stock, paid from the treasury each round, with the existing decay as the default when unpaid; (2) remove the scorer saturation caps once the cost binds; (3) paid heads draw on the region's population pool (civilian population is distinct, GENERATION_STRATEGY § Population is civilian, so this is a levy from it, not a subtraction of it). Treaty break re-scores against a treasury that can now be poor.

DONE WHEN: exploration_sim_harness shows an over-built polity poorer every round and a cap-free allocation that no longer buys an army every round; exploration_sweep reads treaty breaks above the 0.08% baseline and the displacement reading (BL-971's weighted one) does not fall below 1.0; NR-866 resolves. This is a world-moving change under exploration_sim_enabled; digests re-blessed once with the movement described.

items.author: Claude (2026-09-15 generation audit, five parallel readers); Ben chose A) file, B) build the harness library, then build
items.title: Node effects are generated from the tree stores and applied by the sim, replacing the three hand-wired nodes
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-15. gen_empire_tree_table.js emits topology (links, requires, excludes, gate, is_root) and the pursued_when scorer term, and nothing else; grep for "effect" in the script and both generated headers returns nothing. So every minor's modifier, every major's unlock and every milestone's open in both wired trees does nothing. The sim reads exactly three nodes, by hand: rim_node_index = 5 (counted, gates nothing), exploration_sea_legs_node_index = 11 (gates arrival across water), and EX-WY-1a by strcmp (buys the post road). TREES.md:57-58's authoring rule, "a node whose effect nothing in the sim reads is not authored", is unmet for every node.

WORK: (1) extend the generator to emit each node's effects as a static table (kind, target, per_mille, the vocabulary tree_lint already validates); (2) a single apply_tree_effects(polity) in the sim that folds held nodes' modifiers into the polity's modifier surface and unlocks into its verb availability, generically; (3) re-express the three hand-wired nodes as effects in the store and delete the index and string lookups; (4) a harness check per tree that every effect kind in the store has a reader.

DONE WHEN: no node index or id literal remains in history_sim.*; the harness proves every store effect reaches the sim; sweeps re-read (this WILL move the world, because effects that did nothing now do something; the movement is described and re-blessed once).

items.author: Claude (2026-09-15 generation audit, five parallel readers); Ben chose A) file, B) build the harness library, then build
items.title: Nation treasuries are credited from the Exploration treasury at the fold, so garrisons and budgets differentiate
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-15. exploration_output carries a treasury per polity at its capital (BL-932). nation_component::treasury is 0.0 at generation (components.hpp:1750); nation_generation.cpp:1362 says "every garrison lands on min_count today; the scaling only starts to differentiate nations once something credits a treasury, which nothing in the generation chain does yet"; NATION_GENERATION.md § Pass 7 (starting treasury) is ruled and marked not yet implemented. The history writes the number and the campaign reads a zero.

WORK: at the polity fold (nation_generation Pass 2d), sum the folded polities' 1660 treasuries into the nation's starting treasury through one stated conversion (a per-mille of the sim's material currency to campaign money, named in NATION_GENERATION.md § Pass 7 and nowhere else). seed_nation_garrisons then reads a real number. Do not touch what the treasury is spent on; that is Digitisation's.

DONE WHEN: on the reference seed nations start with unequal treasuries traceable to the 1660 table; garrisons differentiate; era_world_harness gains a check that a nation folded from a richer polity starts richer; digests re-blessed once.

items.author: Claude (2026-09-15 generation audit, five parallel readers); Ben chose A) file, B) build the harness library, then build
items.title: The industrial-timing tariff derivation is retired on the single-span arc; the enactment seam stays for Digitisation
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-15. polity::protection_q is derived from industrialisation timing, which only exists when era_minus_one_has_industrial_span (epoch_year >= 1700). The shipped default is epoch_year = 0, so protection_q is 0 everywhere, seed_national_tariffs is a no-op, and the checked-in history_sweep.json shows industrial_first/median/last = 0 on every seed. BL-750's own record was 1 of 8 worlds with any tariff. DIGITISATION.md's boundary table assigns "tariff posture by 1960" to Digitisation.

WORK: remove the industrial-timing derivation from the single-span path (keep it behind the two-span branch, untouched, for the --epoch 1960 arc); keep derive_national_protection and seed_national_tariffs as the enactment seam, reading a protection_q that Digitisation will write from scarcity and flows. Record in DIGITISATION.md § The boundary that the inputs (scarcity, flows, preference) already cross and the derivation is owed there.

DONE WHEN: the shipped arc's behaviour is unchanged (no tariffs, as today) and the code no longer computes a number nothing can use; the 1960 arc digest is unchanged.

items.author: Claude (2026-09-15 generation audit, five parallel readers); Ben chose A) file, B) build the harness library, then build
items.title: The landscape search perturbs a live roster and a scored road tier: the fifth term lands and specialists regenerate
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-15. search_landscape is real and deterministic (fixed rounds, total order, strict improvement) and searches ONE axis live. app.cpp:1013-1026 passes regenerate_specialists = false, so apply_landscape_candidate skips generate_corporations and the roster axis is a no-op. NR-793 measured road tiers 1, 2 and 3 scoring bit-identically on every term, which is why GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § The eight phases added the fifth term, reach quality, on 2026-09-08; landscape_score has four terms and its header still says three. Nineteen evaluations, one axis, ~20 s of startup.

WORK: (1) the reach-quality term as the doc specifies: a per-market reading whose SPREAD is scored, never a global bonus; first slice is the doc's own test, score candidates differing only in road tier and confirm the reading discriminates, choosing between mean traversal cost and in-reach tile count by measurement. (2) regenerate_specialists = true at the live seam, with the corporation seed keyed per (round, axis) as the search already keys its RNG. (3) Fix the header. Cost measured before and after; if the roster axis makes an evaluation expensive, reduce rounds rather than keep an axis that cannot move.

DONE WHEN: the harness shows three road tiers scoring differently and two rosters scoring differently; the search path prints which axis each round's winner came from; startup cost reported.

items.author: Claude (2026-09-15 generation audit, five parallel readers); Ben chose A) file, B) build the harness library, then build
items.title: pre_game_ticks is removed; the landscape search's single validation run is the settle
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-15. BL-772 (retire warm start) was cancelled in the purge with its own record saying the startup drop "reads ZERO SECONDS, recorded as failed rather than quietly dropped". app.cpp:634/639 still arms 80 pre_game_ticks, runs them in slices (:561-584), prints warm_start_80_ticks (:1083) and seeds m_econ_steps from them (:1766). ERAS.md and MARKETS.md were both rewritten to say the warm start is gone. Two docs assert a retirement the code did not do, and phase 6's ~20 s sits on top of the ~72 s it was meant to replace.

WORK: GENERATION_STRATEGY § Three passes: pass 3 SELECTS, it does not settle. Run the winner's one short validation tick-simulation (the doc's "validate dynamically, once") in place of the 80 ticks, keep the balances it produces, and delete pre_game_ticks and the sliced loop. If the validation run must be shorter than 80 ticks to hold the budget, say how short and why in ERAS.md. m_econ_steps starts from the validation run's length.

DONE WHEN: startup time drops by the warm start's measured cost minus the validation run's; haulage_measure stays above the 1055/802 baseline (the only instrument that sees trade); econ goldens re-blessed once with the movement described.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, form on the wave-0 review calls); Claude (filed)
items.title: At 1200 CE every seat a polity holds folds its stores into the capital treasury, as EXPLORATION.md says
items.design:
RULED 2026-09-15 (Ben, NR-871): the doc is right. EXPLORATION.md sec Capital arrives: "At 1200 CE every seat's stores flow to the capital, once." history_sim.cpp's consolidation block at the span's start year does seat.treasury += seat.material_stock; material_stock = 0 for the CAPITAL region only; every other seat the polity holds keeps its material_stock on the ground, unseen by the treasury and the spend scorer.

WORK: at start_year, for every region with is_seat and nation == polity, fold material_stock into the capital's treasury and zero it; non-capital seats then accumulate again as the round runs (the doc's "once"). A world-moving change under exploration_sim_enabled: measure before and after in isolation (exploration_sweep 16, treasury spread and Alarm readings will move), report the movement, do not re-bless. exploration_sim_harness gains a check that a two-seat polity opens with both seats' stock in its treasury and the non-capital seat at 0.

DONE WHEN: the check is green; the sweep movement is described (treasury_spread, readings 7-8) for the wave re-bless.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, form on the wave-0 review calls); Claude (filed)
items.title: Each held seed in the displacement reading gets a named cause before any constant moves
items.design:
RULED 2026-09-15 (Ben, NR-873): measure a cause per held seed before any constant moves. On the integrated wave-0 tree six of sixteen seeds are HELD (neighbour war still leads the frontier): seeds 0, 3, 6, 7, 12, 15 before the schism fix; re-read the set from exploration_sweep.json.

WORK: for each held seed, the sweep prints a cause line from the counters it already has: the share of neighbour campaigns refused by deterrence versus allowed, the share of pairs bound by treaty, whether any polity crossed the explorer rim, the number of frontier candidates in reach (the water gate and the reach gate counters), and the want table's outward share. Classify each held seed as NO FRONTIER (nothing to displace to), NO EXPLORER (no polity holds the rim), TREATY-CALM (neighbours bound, frontier not reachable) or DETERRENCE-INERT (frontier reachable, Alarm never fired). Print the classification on the face and write it into exploration_sweep.json per seed. No constant moves in this item.

DONE WHEN: every held seed carries one of the four causes on the face and in the JSON; a NEEDS_REVIEW entry summarises the census for Ben with the constant each cause would implicate.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, form on the wave-0 review calls); Claude (filed)
items.title: The Empires round leaderboard ranks share of the world by population held, not regions held
items.design:
RULED 2026-09-15 (Ben, NR-876): accept the arc's shape, and the wizard shows the population column. history_sweep now reads every share by population held beside region count (BL-970): by population the largest polities are 2-5 points MORE concentrated (median 10% vs 8%), and rose-and-fell counts drop three times, because most region-count risers were founding empty ground. The round-4 leaderboard (STARTUP.md sec Rounds 4 and 5: "share of the world owned") ranks by regions.

Region share may stay as a second column if it fits the panel; the population one is the rank. Live click required (a UI requirement): open build_rel, run round 4, read the board.

items.title: The per-tile derivation breadcrumb leaves GENERATION_LEDGER.md

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: The thirteen Digitisation readings are instrumented over a seed spread before any mechanism lands
items.design:
DIGITISATION.md § What the phase is judged on lists thirteen readings at 1960 CE, one per opening-map property and beat: density follows cities, cultural stock, advanced chains, live conflict, mixed cities, inequality, far trade, industrialisation, migration, decolonisation, world war (some worlds, never all, never none), war dead (population falls, no region emptied), and catastrophe lean (world-war worlds open with higher aggregate Alarm against Ceiling).

WHY FIRST. The Exploration sprint landed its readings first (BL-937) and it was the reason the frozen-map risk was measurable. Pass 1 grew mechanisms nobody could judge. This phase is designed backwards from its consumer; the readings are that consumer made executable.

DONE WHEN: a harness prints all thirteen over a 16-seed sweep with a spread, not a per-world verdict, and each reading prints n/a honestly until the mechanism it reads exists. Never weaken a reading to pass.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: The Digitisation span runs 1660 → 1960 on the shared engine, taking exploration_output and producing a validated digitisation handoff
items.design:
The fourth span on history_sim, opening where Exploration closes. Its only input is the exploration_output struct (EXPLORATION.md § What this phase hands digitisation); its output is a struct with a validator on the same footing as the Empire and Exploration handoffs, whose fields are DIGITISATION.md § What crosses into play. The Industry tree is the tree invested in, gated behind Exploration's rim.

MEASURE COST FIRST (DIGITISATION.md § Where it will be hard, item 5): 300 years on a region count that grows inside the run, with migration adding per-round work. Report wall-clock per seed against the Exploration span before adding mechanism.

DONE WHEN: world setup reads grudges and corridors from the 1960 handoff where the span ran (the 1660 ones otherwise), the validator runs in production, world_determinism is bit-identical, and history_sim_harness plus exploration_sim_harness stay green.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: Large cities build located industry points, spent on rail, mechanised force or works; the remainder is the charter budget
items.design:
DIGITISATION.md § Beat 1. SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15): three sinks — RAIL (the road ladder's next rung on corridors from the city), MECHANISED FORCE (army and navy stock from industry rather than treasury), WORKS (the city's own yield next round) — and what is unspent at 1960 is the centre's CHARTER BUDGET.

PROPOSED in the doc and carried: one number per population centre, LOCATED (a conqueror takes it); produced from centre scale, fuel within reach (the Industry tree fuel gate), capital paid in from the polity treasury, and Industry tree capacity; the Works fork (State Arsenal spends, Private Works stockpiles) decides the lean as a derived disposition, never a flag.

The spend is an allocation inside the upkeep step, the Exploration idiom (EXPLORATION.md § Force persists now). No term inside the scorer picks a sink for a polity.

DONE WHEN: the industrialisation reading shows industry points unevenly held with the fuel gate visible in who holds them, and both Works-fork sides appear among industrialised polities.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: People and culture shares stream into cities and across borders, and innovation reads urban mass
items.design:
DIGITISATION.md § Beat 2. Two streams on one rule: URBANISATION (countryside to a centre in the same polity) and EMIGRATION (a centre to a centre in another polity), pulled by industry-point output at the destination (the sim holds no wage), pushed by depleted or strained ground, war and a lost colony, carried on a line (held corridors; contact, a line that carries people, no war between the pair).

MIGRATION CARRIES CULTURE SHARES, so population centres gain a culture_shares of their own — the substrate for the culture lens (BL-992) and the cultural demand weight (BL-991).

INNOVATION READS URBAN MASS: Industry tree investment reads the population of a polity's largest centres, superlinearly, on the scorer's one shape (trees/TREES.md § The scorer).

OPEN AND MEASURED: where the pull saturates, so the countryside is not emptied.

DONE WHEN: the migration reading shows urban share rising across the span and a cross-border stream in most worlds, and the mixed-cities reading finds checker-qualifying centres concentrated in large ones.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: Subjects refuse renewal once they can pay for themselves, and holding one grows dearer as its cities grow
items.design:
DIGITISATION.md § Beat 3. Ben, 2026-09-15: "the ability to keep colonies grows harder regardless of whether there is war." Reuses Exploration's tribute-renewal refusal (EXPLORATION.md § A colony is a subject); the refusal score gains the subject's own urban mass and industry points. The overlord's holding cost (garrison upkeep) scales with the subject's population and industry, so the bill grows with no shot fired. NOTHING COUNTS DOWN — no timer, no era flag.

Wars over empire are contests for subjects between powers, on the existing campaign verb. A decolonised polity crosses at 1960 as a nation.

DONE WHEN: the decolonisation reading shows fewer subjects at 1960 than 1660, not zero, with at least one lost without a war in most worlds.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: Industrial war kills through conscript dead, displacement and blockade famine, and never empties a region
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15, notes): "we really need to ensure that people die when wars happen. It's not good for any regime or polity." Takes MILITARY_HISTORY.md's 2026-09-09 exception route — an authored, visible mechanism, never a battle coefficient — and only for the Digitisation span.

THREE MECHANISMS (PROPOSED in the doc): CONSCRIPT DEAD — mechanised force is raised from population, and losses are drawn back from the raising regions in proportion to what each gave; DISPLACEMENT — war ground pushes an emigration stream toward safe cities (BL-985); BLOCKADE FAMINE — interdicted supply thins a civilian count while it stands, bounded by duration and food.

THE DEAD-REGION LOOP MUST STAY SHUT (MILITARY_HISTORY.md: 258 battles, 258 conquests, one region). No loss falls on the battlefield region by being fought over.

RELATED: NR-866 records that paid heads cost no population today; conscript dead makes force cost people for the first time.

COST FOR THE VICTOR: fewer people, smaller cities, fewer industry points; war weariness lowers cohesion and raises every subject's refusal.

DONE WHEN: the war-dead reading shows every war lowering population somewhere and no region emptied, across 16 seeds.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: A war over empire becomes general when the mutual-defence graph draws in the great powers, and leaves the epoch more Alarmed
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15): a world war is PERMITTED, NEVER FORCED — "we don't force it, but it is not unlikely. So I am happy with seeds that reach either target." And a world that fought one is "more likely to fail our Era 1 catastrophe — nuclear war."

PROPOSED MECHANISM: a contest for a subject draws each power's mutual-defence partners, and theirs in turn; how densely the great powers are bound decides whether a colonial war stays local. No scheduled event, no roll.

THE ERA 1 LINK uses ERAS.md's two scalars and no third: standing mechanised force, grudges from the dead and severed flows seed per-nation Alarm at world setup; none of it adds Ceiling. It is not the rupture (HISTORY.md § Stage 5: averted, not past).

DONE WHEN: the world-war reading finds one in some worlds and not others across 16 seeds (never all, never none), and the catastrophe-lean reading shows higher aggregate Alarm against Ceiling on world-war worlds. If the rate is all or nothing, the fix is the treaty graph's causes, never a clamp on the war.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: Great powers back clients in left-behind or decolonised polities, and wars standing at 1960 cross as a province condition
items.design:
DIGITISATION.md § 3. SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15, elicitation): a war standing at the epoch crosses as a STANDING PROVINCE CONDITION — contested ground, interdicted supply, raised ordnance demand, a named patron — resolved by in-world cost, not by an actor choosing moves. NO NEW GRANT: a live nation war would widen AI_OPPONENT.md § 11 and is raised separately if ever wanted.

PROPOSED in the sim: a patron link (a great power paying treasury or force into a client's army), arising where mutual deterrence makes direct war dear — the arms race's next displacement. Nothing picks the client; the price gap does.

WORK SPANS the sim (patron link), the handoff (standing wars and patrons), and the campaign province condition's effect on supply and ordnance demand.

DONE WHEN: the live-conflict reading shows a standing condition in most worlds, most on left-behind or decolonised ground, and a player can see the condition and its patron on the planetary canvas.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: The landscape search spends each city's charter budget, so firm density follows cities
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15, elicitation): Digitisation decides HOW MUCH and WHERE; the search decides WHICH. The search is Digitisation's last act (GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § Round 5 note; DIGITISATION.md § This phase sets budgets; the search spends them). CORPORATION_GENERATION.md § Pass 6 is amended forward: breadth decides which goods a firm serves, the budget decides how many firms stand where.

OWED AND MEASURED: how a budget converts to a firm count, and whether it is spent whole. MEASURE AGAINST TICK COST before tuning density for the map — a dense web is many actors running the corporate scorer every tick.

DONE WHEN: the density reading shows firm count per market rising with catchment urban population rather than good count, and a campaign tick at the seeded density is measured and reported.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: Household demand keeps universal presence and takes a cultural weight from the catchment's peoples
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15, elicitation): MARKETS.md § Three properties the set has to hold, property 5, AMENDED — every market keeps a buyer for every terminal good its band supports; the VOLUME of household demand for a good is weighted by the population-weighted preference of the culture shares across the catchment (region and centre shares). Preference is Exploration's derived per-culture weight, carried to 1960.

ALSO SEEDED HERE: the starting price per market from the scarcity signal, inside the band (DIGITISATION.md Part III).

DONE WHEN: the cultural-stock reading shows the most-preferred goods with a local or preferred seller in most markets, and two markets on one world show different household demand for the same good for a reason the culture lens can show.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: A culture lens fills provinces with the primary culture and checkers the second where it is within 95%
items.design:
LENSES.md § Culture lens. SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15): primary culture per province as a blended lineage-hue fill; a HARD CHECKER of the top two where the second share is at least 95% OF THE FIRST (relative: 42/40 checkers, 42/38 does not). Only the top two draw. The checker is the one exception to PROVINCES.md § Every lens blends across provinces.

DATA: province culture is DERIVED (PROVINCES.md § What a province is, amended) — region rural shares blended with each inside centre's shares, population-weighted; nothing stored on the province. Reuses palette::lineage_colour (BL-919).

QUESTION (required on every surface): "Who lives here, and so what does this market want?" — add the question_log entry and the ui_elements row.

DONE WHEN: a verifier-visual capture shows plain countryside and checkered cities on a Digitisation world, AND a live click in the built app arms the lens and reads a checkered province (a UI requirement needs a live check).

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: Nations read GDP, markets read listed value, and inequality reads as spreads between nations and cities
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15, elicitation). GDP (NATIONS.md § GDP): valued production on a nation's tiles at local prices, derived, trailing window in play, capacity at the seeded price field at the epoch; promotes NR-774's tool-only definition. LISTED VALUE (MARKETS.md § A market's listed value): summed buyout valuation of firms headquartered in the catchment — a sum over firms, no equity, no share price. INEQUALITY: GDP per head across nations and output per centre within one, read never stored, never households.

One shared implementation for the harness reading and the player surface, so a check never measures something different from the screen.

DONE WHEN: the inequality reading shows wide spreads on both axes, and the nation and market surfaces show GDP and listed value with a live click.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: The epoch seeds stub campaign tech, a regime field and garrison strength from the Digitisation handoff
items.design:
DIGITISATION.md § 6, SET (Ben, 2026-09-15): "very simple stubs for now." TECH: the Industry tree mask sets the campaign tree's starting unlocks per nation (The Renewed Line opens it). REGIME: one field beside the three character enums, derived from the Works fork, charter reach, subject history and whether the polity fought a world war; invented names only. GARRISONS: sized from carried army_stock, navy and mechanised force, not from a treasury seeded at zero.

Stubs mean one field each with a named source; nothing reads the regime in play yet.

DONE WHEN: two nations on one world open with different tech state, regime and garrison strength traceable to their history, and the save round-trips the new fields.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: Campaign trade chases price over distance: a seller can reach a far market, and sea is cheap per distance at bulk
items.design:
DESIGN OWED. The opening-map property most at risk (DIGITISATION.md § 7 and § Where it will be hard, item 1): Ben, 2026-09-15, wants "working international markets, where often it will be better to send materials overseas — or over distance on land — than to send materials to the closest market." Generation can seed price gaps; five campaign rules erase or ignore them: one base_price per good everywhere; a tile sells to its NEAREST market; dispatch chases SHORTFALL not price; sea costs MORE per distance than land; tariffs fire only on matched order-book trades whose buy side has no emitter.

THE QUESTIONS FOR A DESIGN SESSION on MARKETS.md and SUPPLY.md: may a seller route to a non-catchment market by landed price; is sea per-distance cheaper than land at bulk (the real mechanism); do tariffs act on every cross-border sale; does the 10x ceiling derivation (nearest-neighbour haul) still hold.

DONE WHEN (once designed): the far-trade reading holds at the epoch AND after a year of play — a gap play erases in a year was never a working international market.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: Household demand ladders with centre stratum, so advanced goods have a buyer before the epoch seeds their sellers
items.design:
DESIGN OWED. DIGITISATION.md § 2: advanced production at the epoch needs a buyer. POPULATION.md states that demand ladders with stratum (a metropolis pulls electronics) but no basket authors it, and most industrial demand is a world-scale background stopgap. Seeding electronics and machinery installations without it reproduces the idle-at-the-ceiling failure that killed the industrial field.

OWED: the per-stratum basket for the industrial band — which goods each stratum adds, and at what volume — authored against the recipe-margin anchor.

DONE WHEN (once designed): electronics and machinery clear against household demand in metropolis-scale markets without the stopgap carrying them.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: Wizard round 6 is a 1660 → 1960 time-lapse of the three beats that closes on the seeded opening map
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15, elicitation): STARTUP.md § Rounds, round 6 — a time-lapse on the same 2D map as rounds 3–5 showing industrialisation (cities lighting, rail spreading), mass migration (streams into cities, their culture tint turning mixed) and decolonisation (subjects standing up, wars over empire flaring, one sometimes general), closing on the epoch's opening map with firms and the market carve drawn in place. Replaces the placeholder and the still-globe specification.

Same contract as rounds 3–5: write-only tap, playhead lags the calculation at a constant rate (~30 s span), scrubbable once landed, causal reroll, no Run button.

DONE WHEN: a live click through the wizard reaches round 6, watches the three beats and lands on the seeded map, and a watched and unwatched run are byte-identical.
